title: Does Fine-Tuning for Helpfulness Reduce Safety Diversity?

original_idea.title: Does Fine-Tuning for Helpfulness Reduce Safety Diversity?
original_idea.problem: RLHF is known to reduce output diversity generally; it is unknown whether this reduction is especially pronounced for safety-relevant outputs.
original_idea.direction: Compare base models vs. RLHF-tuned counterparts on a standardized safety prompt set, measuring diversity of refusal styles, reasoning chains, and edge-case handling.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If alignment fine-tuning homogenizes safety outputs, the very process meant to make models safe may simultaneously make the ecosystem more brittle.
original_idea.relevant_context: RLHF significantly reduces diversity vs. SFT (arXiv 2310.06452, ICLR 2024). Artificial Hivemind shows inter-model homogeneity is a persistent phenomenon.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reduced from 4 to 3. The core finding (RLHF reduces diversity) is already well-established. The safety-specific angle adds value but the fundamental tension is already documented.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: comparing base vs. RLHF-tuned model variants on safety prompts requires some setup with open-source models but is feasible with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: controlled comparison of base vs. tuned model pairs on a fixed safety prompt set with clear diversity metrics.

novelty.reasoning: The RLHF diversity reduction effect is well-established. 'Understanding the Effects of RLHF on LLM Generalisation and Diversity' (ICLR 2024) showed RLHF significantly reduces output diversity vs. SFT. A 2025 study confirmed RL algorithms converge toward dominant output distributions. 'Homogenizing Effect of LLMs on Cognitive Diversity' (2025, arxiv 2508.01491) further documents homogenization. The specific angle of measuring whether diversity reduction is more pronounced for safety-relevant outputs is partially novel, but the core finding (RLHF reduces diversity) is already established.
